sections.title: Why study Automobile Engineering in France?
sections.lead: The design, development, testing, manufacturing, and enhancement of automobiles and their systems is referred to as automobile engineering.

items: In France you can study traditional automotive technologies as well as \\electric mobility, hybrid propulsion, connected vehicles and sustainable transportation\.
\\Automotive industry exposure:\\ Students can learn about vehicle manufacturers, automotive suppliers, research centers and mobility technology companies.
\\Practical engineering education:\\ The courses may include lab work, design projects, vehicle testing and industrial internships.
Electric vehicle technologies: Relevant topics are battery systems, electric motors, power electronics and energy management.
\\Specialised study:\\ Students can specialize in \\vehicle dynamics, automotive design, propulsion, manufacturing or autonomous systems.

\\International career opportunities:\\ The skills you learn in automotive engineering are transferable to the vehicle manufacturing industry, the automotive supply industry, motorsport, research and transport technology.
Students need to be well versed in \\mathematics, physics, mechanics and computing\\ to be prepared for the technical demands of the field.

sections.title: Automotive Engineering Courses in France
sections.lead: The exact name of a \\automotive engineering course in France\\ varies from one French school to another. Useful alternatives include:

items: \\Automotive Engineering:\\ Design of vehicles, vehicle systems, automotive mechanics, testing and manufacturing.
\\Mechanical Engineering:\\ Mechanics, machine design, materials, manufacturing processes, vehicle parts.
\\Automotive and Aeronautical Design:\\ Engineering design methods for transportation systems, including automotive applications.
\\Vehicle Dynamics & Control:\\ Suspension, steering, handling, vehicle stability & control.
\\Electric and Hybrid Vehicle Engineering:\\ Electric drive, energy conversion, battery technology, power management.
\\ Automotive Manufacturing Engineering:\\ Production systems, quality management, industrial automation and manufacturing optimization.
\\Connected and Autonomous Vehicles:\\ Sensor systems, embedded systems, vehicle-to-vehicle communication, autonomous driving technologies.

A \\three-year bachelor's degree\\ is usually worth \\180 ECTS credits\. However many specialist French automotive engineering schools offer a \\five year pathway after secondary school\\ with a two year preparatory cycle and a three year engineering cycle.
A \\mechanical engineering bachelor's degree\\ can also serve as a starting point for future specialization in automotive engineering.

For courses taught in French, a \\ B2-level French \\ is a useful planning benchmark, but the actual requirement depends on the institution. You may need to take an approved \\English language test\\ for programs taught in English.

sections.title: Cost of Studying Automobile Engineering in France
sections.lead: \\Cost of Studying Automobile Engineering in France\\ The cost of studying automobile engineering in France depends on the type of institution, the degree you choose to pursue, your nationality and whether you can get exemptions on tuition.

items: Tuition Rates 2026-2027
The indicative tuition fees for public higher education institutions under the relevant national legislation are published by Campus France as follows:
Public university Licence \| €178/year \| €2,902/year
Master's degree Public university \| €255 per year \| €3,950 per year
Many public engineering programs \| €630 per year \| Ask the school for the rate

The rates indicated are only indicative and are not the fees charged by all institutions. Some engineering schools have their own fee structures and there may be exemptions for eligible international students.
Private schools may charge a lot more tuition.
Students need to set aside money for:
\\Housing and utilities.
\\Food and grocery shopping.
\\Transport local.
Engineering books, software and study material.
Health-related costs and insurance where appropriate.
\\Visa and administration fees.
The \\cost of living in France\\ will depend on the city, your housing situation and your lifestyle. Living in Paris or another big city costs more than living in a smaller university town.
Scholarships, financial aid and eligible work-study arrangements\\ may reduce costs depending on the program and the student's circumstances.

sections.title: Admissions Process
sections.lead: International applicants should follow the institution's application route and relevant French higher educational procedures.

items: 1. \\Select your course:\\ Choose from a \\bachelor's degree, a preparatory cycle, or a complete engineering qualification\.
2. \\Check institutions:\\ Look at course content, duration, medium of instruction, tuition fees and degree recognition.
3. \\Check eligibility:\\ Check the required academic subjects, grades and language requirements.
4. \\Choose the platform:\\ Schools can use \\Parcours, Études en France\\ or their own platform depending on the school and the applicant category.
5. \\Documents to prepare:\\ Collect certificates, transcripts, passport details and language-test results.
6. \\Apply\\: Fill out all forms and submit them before the deadline for the program you're applying to.
7. \\Complete selection stages: Appear for any entrance test or interview as per the requirement of the school.

sections.title: Accreditation and Recognition
sections.lead: Students should ensure that the qualification they have chosen is \\recognised and appropriate for their career goals\\ before enrolling.

items: The \Diplôme d'ingénieur\ is a recognized engineering qualification in France, if it is conferred by a program that is authorized by the appropriate French authorities after undergoing the \\Commission des titres d'ingénieur (CTI) accreditation process\.
Please read the details below before applying:
The \\exact degree or diploma\\ that is awarded.
Whether the program is \\CTI accredited\\, where applicable.
Duration of the course and \\credits (ECTS).
Availability of internships, practical training & industry projects.
Opportunities for postgraduate study or professional recognition overseas.
A \\bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering\\ is not equivalent to a recognized engineering diploma. Students should not expect to have the same professional or academic outcomes.

faqs.q: \\ Can I do automobile engineering in France after 12th?
faqs.a: Yes. Some engineering schools have a \\preparatory cycle\\ which begins after secondary school and leads to an engineering qualification. You could also look into \\bachelor's programs in mechanical engineering\\ which provide a base for automotive specialization.

faqs.q: How many years is automobile engineering in France ?
faqs.a: A \\bachelor's programme\\ usually lasts three years. The full \\engineering-school pathway\\ usually lasts five years after high school, often with two years of pre-university studies and three years of engineering studies.

faqs.q: Do they teach automobile engineering in English in France?
faqs.a: The language of instruction depends on the institution and the program. Many of the undergraduate engineering tracks are taught primarily in French, while a choice of international programs and graduate level courses are taught in English. Please check the current language requirements before you apply.

faqs.q: What is the cost of automobile engineering in France?
faqs.a: \\Tuition fees for automobile engineering in France\\ depend on the institution and the level of qualification. The reference fees for Licence at public universities for 2026-2027 are €178 per year for French and EU students who meet the conditions and €2,902 for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. Fees may vary between engineering schools and private institutions.

faqs.q: What jobs are available after Automobile Engineering?
faqs.a: You could pursue a career in \\automotive design, vehicle testing, electric vehicle systems, manufacturing, powertrain engineering, quality assurance, or research and development. Some specialist roles require a diploma in engineering or further study.
